2.0.0. Telnet Service Enabled.ease: High — Sniffing tools are widely available and extremely easy to use.
2.0.0. Telnet Service Enabled.impact: An attacker who is able to sniff network traffic can easily capture administrative credentials in transit.
2.0.0. Telnet Service Enabled.observation: The Telnet service is currently enabled on the device. Telnet is an insecure, clear-text protocol and does not encrypt management traffic.
2.0.0. Telnet Service Enabled.recommendation: It is strongly recommended to disable Telnet access using 'no telnet ...' and use SSH for encrypted remote management.
2.0.0. Telnet Service Enabled.title: Telnet Service Enabled

2.0.1. Weak Enable Password Configured.ease: High — Weak passwords are highly susceptible to dictionary and automated brute-force attacks.
2.0.1. Weak Enable Password Configured.impact: An attacker who gets user-level access can guess the enable password and obtain full administrative control over the firewall.
2.0.1. Weak Enable Password Configured.observation: The enable password 'cisco123' is weak, common, or easily guessable.
2.0.1. Weak Enable Password Configured.recommendation: Change the enable password to a complex value using the command: enable password <complex_password>
2.0.1. Weak Enable Password Configured.title: Weak Enable Password Configured

2.0.2. Insecure SNMP Community String.ease: High — SNMP brute force scanners will automatically test default community strings.
2.0.2. Insecure SNMP Community String.impact: An attacker can read (public) or modify (private) system configuration and status via SNMP, exposing sensitive info.
2.0.2. Insecure SNMP Community String.observation: The device has an insecure SNMP community string 'public' configured.
2.0.2. Insecure SNMP Community String.recommendation: Change community strings to a private complex value: snmp-server community <complex_string>
2.0.2. Insecure SNMP Community String.title: Insecure SNMP Community String

2.0.3. Unrestricted SSH Access Enabled.ease: Medium — Requires credentials to exploit, but massively increases exposure.
2.0.3. Unrestricted SSH Access Enabled.impact: Exposes the SSH management interface to password guessing and potential zero-day exploit attempts from unauthorized hosts.
2.0.3. Unrestricted SSH Access Enabled.observation: SSH access is configured with 0.0.0.0/0, allowing access from any IP address on the network/internet.
2.0.3. Unrestricted SSH Access Enabled.recommendation: Restrict SSH access to trusted administration subnets using 'ssh <ip> <mask> <interface>'.
2.0.3. Unrestricted SSH Access Enabled.title: Unrestricted SSH Access Enabled

2.0.4. Logging Disabled or Missing Confi.ease: Low — Does not directly allow penetration, but severely cripples security operations and compliance.
2.0.4. Logging Disabled or Missing Confi.impact: Without logs, it is impossible to detect security incidents, perform audit trails, or conduct forensic analysis after a breach.
2.0.4. Logging Disabled or Missing Confi.observation: System logging is not enabled on this firewall ('no logging enable' is active).
2.0.4. Logging Disabled or Missing Confi.recommendation: Enable logging and configure a secure external syslog host: logging enable; logging host <interface> <ip>
2.0.4. Logging Disabled or Missing Confi.title: Logging Disabled or Missing Configuration

2.0.5. Insecure SSL/TLS Version Configur.ease: Medium — Interception of admin management sessions can reveal login credentials.
2.0.5. Insecure SSL/TLS Version Configur.impact: TLS 1.0, 1.1, and SSLv3 have known cryptographic vulnerabilities (e.g. POODLE, BEAST) that can lead to session decryption.
2.0.5. Insecure SSL/TLS Version Configur.observation: The firewall's minimum SSL/TLS version is configured as 'tlsv1'.
2.0.5. Insecure SSL/TLS Version Configur.recommendation: Configure TLS 1.2 as the minimum version: ssl minimum-version tlsv1.2
2.0.5. Insecure SSL/TLS Version Configur.title: Insecure SSL/TLS Version Configured

2.0.6. Wide Open ACL Rule on Outside Int.ease: Critical — Allows immediate access/attack vector to all internal resources.
2.0.6. Wide Open ACL Rule on Outside Int.impact: Allows unrestricted inbound network traffic from any source to any destination, defeating the primary firewall security boundary.
2.0.6. Wide Open ACL Rule on Outside Int.observation: ACL 'outside_access_in' on low-security interface 'outside' contains a wide-open rule: 'access-list outside_access_in extended permit ip any any'
2.0.6. Wide Open ACL Rule on Outside Int.recommendation: Restrict the ACL to only permit traffic to authorized hosts/ports: permit tcp any host <ip> eq <port>
2.0.6. Wide Open ACL Rule on Outside Int.title: Wide Open ACL Rule on Outside Interface

2.1.0. Missing Logging Configuration.ease: Without logs, unauthorized access or configuration changes may go undetected.
2.1.0. Missing Logging Configuration.impact: Lack of logs makes it difficult to investigate security incidents or troubleshoot issues.
2.1.0. Missing Logging Configuration.observation: System logging is not enabled on the device.
2.1.0. Missing Logging Configuration.recommendation: Enable system logging. Command: logging enable
2.1.0. Missing Logging Configuration.title: Missing Logging Configuration

2.2.0. Telnet Enabled.ease: It is trivial to use captured credentials to log in.
2.2.0. Telnet Enabled.impact: An attacker could capture authentication credentials monitoring network traffic.
2.2.0. Telnet Enabled.observation: The Telnet service is enabled on the device. Telnet is a clear-text protocol and is vulnerable to packet-capture techniques.
2.2.0. Telnet Enabled.recommendation: Disable Telnet and use SSH instead. Command: no telnet <network> <mask> <interface>
2.2.0. Telnet Enabled.title: Telnet Enabled

2.2.1. Unrestricted SSH Access.ease: Attackers can attempt to guess passwords from any network location.
2.2.1. Unrestricted SSH Access.impact: Increases the risk of brute-force attacks from unauthorized hosts.
2.2.1. Unrestricted SSH Access.observation: SSH access is allowed from any IP address (0.0.0.0).
2.2.1. Unrestricted SSH Access.recommendation: Restrict SSH access to specific management networks. Command: ssh <management-network> <mask> <interface>
2.2.1. Unrestricted SSH Access.title: Unrestricted SSH Access

2.3.0. Insecure SNMP Communities.ease: Common community strings are widely known and frequently targeted by automated scanners.
2.3.0. Insecure SNMP Communities.impact: Attackers can easily guess these strings to gain information or modify configuration via SNMP.
2.3.0. Insecure SNMP Communities.observation: The SNMP service is configured with common or default community strings (e.g., 'public', 'private').
2.3.0. Insecure SNMP Communities.recommendation: Change SNMP community strings to complex, unique values. Command: snmp-server community <new-string>
2.3.0. Insecure SNMP Communities.title: Insecure SNMP Communities
